motion: The U.S. Should Adopt the 'Right to Be Forgotten' Online

dropped_turns.speaker: PRO
dropped_turns.text: Your weakest claim is that context solves the problem. Search snippets and hostile reposts rarely deliver context before a reader judges someone. A right to challenge irrelevant results addresses that first impression, so adoption is justified.

dropped_turns.speaker: CON
dropped_turns.text: On your first-impression point, removal is a blunt cure for a real problem. People can answer false or unfair material, and platforms can improve labels and ranking. Government-backed hiding of truthful records risks more harm, so reject the motion.

dropped_turns.speaker: PRO
dropped_turns.text: A parent may have an old personal photo attached to a humiliating rumor that resurfaces whenever a child searches their name. The parent cannot realistically answer every copy forever. Removal from major searches restores dignity, proving we should adopt it.

dropped_turns.speaker: CON
dropped_turns.text: I grant that dignity matters when old material resurfaces. But a sweeping legal right invites endless disputes over relevance and truth, burdening speakers and readers. Narrow voluntary remedies are better than adopting the motion.
